newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Thai premier seeks to boost ties with Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Thai premier seeks to boost ties with Vietnam.

text.p: Visiting Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh pledged closer economic ties with Vietnam on Sunday as well as efforts to iron out long-standing differences over maritime boundaries and fishing rights.
Chavalit, whose official visit began in Hanoi with a ceremonial welcome and a downpour of rain, later held talks with Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet and Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi.

Thai diplomats said the issue of competing claims in the Gulf of Thailand, where the Thai and Vietnamese continental shelves overlap for about 6,000 sq km (2.300 sq miles), was only mentioned briefly, as was the possibility of shared fishing rights.
However, Chavalit's 24-hour visit was aimed at paving the way for joint meetings in May on those and other bilateral issues.
Fishermen from the two countries have sometimes clashed or been detained in the past. However, no fishermen are currently being held on either side.

Chavalit, on his third official visit to the communist country but his first as prime minister, told the Vietnam News Agency (VNA) last week that maritime sovereignty disputes were "a minor irritant" in overall good relations.
He told a news conference later that trade and investment ties were important, not just for the bilateral benefits but also for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

VNA said trade between the two ASEAN countries rose by $100 million in 1996 to $610 million and was expected to reach the $1-billion-dollar mark this year. Thailand ranks 19th among foreign investors in Vietnam, committing about $1.2 billion for 74 projects.

Chavalit said Kiet had agreed to ease the way for Thailand to open more bank branches in Vietnam and the two sides agreed to increase the number of flights between Bangkok and Ho Chi Minh City from seven a week to nine.
Asked how he stood on the row between Hanoi and Beijing over Chinese drilling for oil in a South China Sea area that both countries claim, Chavalit said it was not for Thailand to judge.
"ASEAN countries want to see settlement of the dispute in a peaceful way," he said. "Right or wrong it's not for Thailand to judge."
Chavalit is due to visit China on Tuesday.
